description: Knights Corner (K1OM, IMCI) architecture rules shared by every card. Holds documented values and literature values only. Card profiles override with measured values and carry card-specific parameters (clock, cores, bandwidth).

sources.R01: Intel, Xeon Phi Coprocessor System Software Developers Guide, 328207-001EN, Nov 2012 (local: .work/_shared/knc-refs/ssdg-2012.pdf)
sources.R02: R. Rahman, Intel Xeon Phi Coprocessor Architecture and Tools, Apress 2013, chapters 3-4; https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4302-5927-5_4
sources.R04: M. Cornea, Numerical Computation on Intel Xeon Phi Coprocessors, 2013 (local: knc-refs/cornea-2013.pdf)
sources.R06: Z. Fang et al., Measuring Microarchitectural Details of Multi- and Many-Core Memory Systems through Microbenchmarking, TACO 11(4) 2014; https://zhenman.github.io/files/J1-TACO2015-uBench-XeonPhi.pdf (pre-production engineering sample, 1 GHz)
sources.R08: J. McCalpin, Native Computing and Optimization on the Intel Xeon Phi Coprocessor, IXPUG 2014; https://www.ixpug.org/docs/IXPUG_2014_MIC_Native-new.pdf (SE10P)
sources.R17: M. Klemm, The Intel Xeon Phi Coprocessor, LMU seminar 2014-12-11, slides 10-14 (local: knc-refs/klemm-microarch-2014.pdf)
sources.R27: Intel, Xeon Phi Coprocessor Instruction Set Architecture Reference Manual, 327364-001, Sept 2012
sources.RAU94: B. R. Rau, Iterative Modulo Scheduling, HPL-94-115; https://shiftleft.com/mirrors/www.hpl.hp.com/techreports/94/HPL-94-115.pdf
sources.SDM: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, vol. 1, sections 4.9.1.5 and 10.2.3.3 (FTZ/DAZ semantics)

core.issue_width.unit: instructions per core cycle (U then V)

core.min_issue_gap_same_context.unit: cycles between two issue events of one context
core.min_issue_gap_same_context.source: R02 ch.4 ('not possible to issue instructions from the same context in back-to-back cycles'); R17 slide 11; consistent with S6-03 measured 2.08 ticks per independent op at one thread

core.picker.source: R02 ch.4 (picker is round robin among ready contexts); R17 slide 10 ('smart round robin')
core.picker.uncertainty: The 'smart' refinement is not documented in detail; the model uses least-recently-issued-first among eligible contexts.

core.decode_bubble_on_unsynchronized_ref.source: R02 ch.4 mentions a one-clock bubble when picker and prefetch-buffer refill are not synchronized (e.g. after an I-cache miss)
core.decode_bubble_on_unsynchronized_ref.note: Not modeled. Instruction fetch is assumed always to hit.

pairing.v_eligible_classes.unit: instruction classes that may issue on the V pipe
pairing.v_eligible_classes.source: R02 p.34 Table 3-1 (mask, vector store, packstore, prefetch, scalar); R17 slide 10 (scalar dual issue)
pairing.v_eligible_classes.uncertainty: Table 3-1 lists mnemonics; the class mapping here is the model's. Ordinary vector arithmetic is U-only. S6-03 pair.vector_vector (4.09 at one thread) confirms two vector arithmetic ops do not pair.

pairing.encoding_rules.note: Applied only when a record carries encoding hints (encoding.bytes, encoding.disp32, encoding.imm). Without hints the model assumes the encoding is pairable and records that assumption.

pairing.dependent_pairs_allowed.unit: U/V pairs allowed despite a flag dependency
pairing.dependent_pairs_allowed.source: R02 p.56 (cmp/jcc, push/push, pop/pop); push/pop not modeled

pairing.u_instruction_can_be_branch.source: model assumption: an instruction after a control transfer in the same issue slot is not paired

latency.scalar_alu.unit: cycles, result ready for a dependent scalar instruction
latency.scalar_alu.uncertainty: S6-03 scalar_add.lat 2.08 at one thread only bounds it at <=2 because of the issue gap.

latency.scalar_imul.source: R02 p.56 (imul executes in the x87 unit, 10 cycles)
latency.scalar_imul.uncertainty: Not measured on the owner's card by the imported characterization.

latency.mask_op.source: Mask ops execute in the scalar pipeline class per R02 Table 3-1; S6-03 kand.lat/kmov.lat 2.08 at one thread bounds it at <=2

latency.vector_arith.source: R17 slide 12 ('most vector operations: 4-cycle latency, 1-cycle throughput'); R02 ch.3 VPU pipeline

latency.vector_long.source: R02 pp.32-33 describes longer swizzle/EMU paths without a number
latency.vector_long.note: Card profiles with measurements set this; the common profile leaves it unknown on purpose so a simulation of these ops without a measured profile stops with missing_parameter.

latency.vector_convert_df.source: R02 p.33 (DP pipeline paths are longer)

latency.scalar_load_l1.unit: cycles, L1 hit load to dependent use (scalar)
latency.scalar_load_l1.source: R08 cache slide ('1 cycle latency for scalar loads'); R17 slide 13 ('1 cycle') vs slide 14 ('2 cycle')
latency.scalar_load_l1.uncertainty: Documented values disagree; the owner's card measured 3 (card-7120-measured overrides).

latency.vector_load_l1.unit: cycles, L1 hit vector load to dependent use
latency.vector_load_l1.source: R08 cache slide ('3 cycles for vector loads')
latency.vector_load_l1.uncertainty: S6-03 masked_load.lat measured 12 on a dependent chain of memory-operand forms; see card-7120-measured.

latency.l2_hit.uncertainty: Literature measurements: R06 §5.1.1 22-23 cycles; R08 ~25 idle; owner's card 24-26 (card-7120-measured).

latency.memory.unit: cycles, idle demand miss to memory
latency.memory.source: Depends on clock and board. R08: ~275-280 ns (~300 cycles on SE10P); R06 §5.1.1: 318-346 cycles at 1 GHz engineering sample; R17 slide 13: about 275 ns
latency.memory.note: Card profiles set it. Left unknown here so a memory-level simulation needs a card profile.

latency.remote_l2_line_ns.unit: ns, read of a line held in another core's L2
latency.remote_l2_line_ns.source: R08: ~275 ns average, independent of core distance; R06 §5.1.2: ~243 cycles average, sd 32 (engineering sample)

latency.agi_cycles.unit: cycles from the issue of a write to a register until it can be used as an address
latency.agi_cycles.source: R01 p.19 (three-clock address setup); R17 slide 13 (3-cycle address-generation interlock)
latency.agi_cycles.uncertainty: S6-03 point 7: a load right after its address write costs one extra tick at one thread, consistent with 3 (issue gap 2 + 1).

latency.branch_taken_bubble.unit: extra cycles after a correctly predicted taken branch
latency.branch_taken_bubble.source: S6-03 C9: a loop costs about 2 ticks per vector op plus 2 per loop branch at one thread, i.e. the branch costs its issue slot only

latency.branch_mispredict_penalty.source: R02 ch.4 does not give a number; S8-01 C10 measured about 5 extra ticks per pseudorandom branch at one thread on the owner's card (rate not separated)
latency.branch_mispredict_penalty.note: Card profiles may set it; scenarios that mispredict need it.

occupancy.x87_mul.unit: core cycles the x87 multiplier is busy

occupancy.x87_div.unit: core cycles the x87 divider is busy

latency.fence.unit: cycles until a lock-prefixed read-modify-write or fence retires
latency.fence.source: not documented; microcode/locked instructions do not pair (R02 p.56)

latency.gather_first_line.unit: cycles until a one-line vgatherd* result is ready
latency.gather_first_line.source: R02 p.32 describes the scatter/gather pipeline; no number

occupancy.gather_cycles_per_line.unit: core cycles both pipes are busy per distinct cache line gathered

occupancy.vprefetch_l2_core_cycles.unit: core cycles between two vprefetch1/2 issues
occupancy.vprefetch_l2_core_cycles.source: no documented limit; S8-01 C2 measured about 2.25 on the owner's card (card-7120-measured overrides)

l1.replacement.source: R17 slide 13 says pseudo-LRU; the model uses true LRU and records the difference as an assumption

l1.accesses_per_cycle.unit: L1 data accesses per core cycle (loads and stores, not prefetches)
l1.accesses_per_cycle.source: R17 slide 13 ('1 access per clock, read or write')
l1.accesses_per_cycle.uncertainty: R02 p.55 describes U and V accessing memory in one cycle with bank-conflict delays, which implies two accesses are possible.

l1.outstanding_demand_misses_per_core.source: R08 concurrency slide ('each core can only support 8 outstanding L1 Data Cache misses')
l1.outstanding_demand_misses_per_core.uncertainty: R01 p.19 gives about 38 combined requests; R06 §5.2.2 measures MSHRs on an engineering sample.

l1.demand_load_miss_stalls_context.source: R08 cache performance notes ('In-order design stalls thread on L1 Data Cache Misses (except for store misses); other threads on the same core can continue'); R02 ch.4 (thread-specific flush on a miss)

l1.software_prefetch_blocks.source: R27 pp.641-656 (prefetch hints have no architectural effect); R08 (software prefetch is the way to tolerate L2 latency)

l2.hardware_prefetcher.source: R01 p.19 (16-stream L2 prefetcher); R08 (strides up to 2 lines, ~24 lines per core); no L1 hardware prefetcher
l2.hardware_prefetcher.note: The model does not simulate the L2 hardware prefetcher. A scenario that relies on it must say so and is reported as unsupported.

l2.outstanding_prefetches_per_core.source: R06 §5.2.2 measured on an engineering sample; not imported as a production constant

vpu.masking.source: R27 (IMCI write masks merge; there is no zeroing form)

vpu.throughput_per_core.source: R17 slide 12 (1-cycle throughput); S6-03 point 1 (two threads reach one vector op per cycle)

fp.sp_denormals_supported.source: R04 slides 9 and 18 ('Denormals are supported by Intel IMCI (but slow, like host)')

fp.ftz_daz_default.source: R27 §2.4 p.39 (MXCSR FTZ/DAZ bits, architectural default clear); R04 slide 18 (Intel compilers set FTZ at -O1 and above)
fp.ftz_daz_default.note: The kernel's numerical_policy decides; this is only the default when the kernel does not say.

fp.ftz_rule.source: SDM vol.1 §10.2.3.3: with FTZ set and underflow masked, a tiny result is replaced by a signed zero; whether an exact tiny result is also flushed is not stated for KNC (R27 §2.4 defines the MXCSR bits only)
fp.ftz_rule.note: The kernel's numerical_policy.ftz_rule can select the alternative.

fp.nan_propagation.source: x86 SSE convention (SDM vol.1 §4.8.3.5); KNC-specific documentation not located
fp.nan_propagation.note: Expected-output comparison treats any NaN as matching any NaN unless numerical_policy.nan_compare is 'bits'.

card.usable_cores.note: card-specific; the OS core is usually excluded

card.ring_bandwidth_gbs.uncertainty: Not used by any current model term; informational.
